The part-of relations are expressed as subclass axioms (universal restrictions at the class level) following standard BFO practice for necessary parthood. Open questions flag potential refinements around additional phases, boundary vs. process typing, and linkage to existing working classes.

entities.label: ContractFormationProcess

relations.rationale: BFO_0000054 (realized in) links a Disposition to the Process in which it is realized. The utterance directly asserts that consideration (a disposition) is realized in the formation process.
Consideration is typed as a subclass of BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016).
ContractFormationProcess is typed as a subclass of BFO Process (BFO_0000015).
BFO_0000055 (realizes) is the inverse of BFO_0000054; the formation process realizes consideration. Adding the inverse as a class-level relation supports reasoner consistency.

The relation BFO_0000054 (realized in) connects the disposition class Consideration to the process class ContractFormationProcess, with the inverse BFO_0000055 (realizes) also asserted for completeness. proposal.utterance: A breach of contract is a process that disrupts the enduring obligation relation.

entities.label: BreachOfContract
entities.rationale: A breach of contract is a kind of happening or event in time — an occurrent process in which an obligor fails to perform a contractual duty. Typed as BFO_0000015 (Process).

entities.label: ContractualObligation
entities.rationale: A contractual obligation is a species of LegalObligation (already in ontology, typed as Role/BFO_0000023). It is an externally-grounded specifically-dependent continuant that inheres in the bearer (the contracting party). Subclassing existing working:LegalObligation is preferred over minting a new top-level class.

entities.label: ObligationDisruption
entities.rationale: The 'disruption' of the enduring obligation relation is modeled as a quality that inheres in the ContractualObligation — specifically, a measurable deviation from the normative state of the obligation. This captures the ontological change-of-state aspect without positing a new process.

relations.rationale: BreachOfContract is a subclass of Process (BFO_0000015), consistent with the utterance asserting it is a process.
ContractualObligation is a species of the existing LegalObligation class, which is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role).
ObligationDisruption is a Quality (BFO_0000019) that characterizes the state of a ContractualObligation when a breach occurs.
A BreachOfContract process has as participant the ContractualObligation that is being disrupted — using RO_0000057 (has participant) to relate the process to the relevant continuant.
ObligationDisruption inheres in (RO_0000052) the ContractualObligation whose enduring relation is disrupted.

open_questions: Should 'ContractualObligation' be modeled purely as a Role (BFO_0000023, externally grounded) or also as a Disposition (BFO_0000016, internally grounded capacity to perform)? The utterance focuses on the 'enduring obligation relation', which may favor Role.

Is 'ObligationDisruption' better modeled as a Quality (a state of the obligation after breach) or as a second Process that is part of BreachOfContract? The utterance says the breach 'disrupts' the relation, which could imply a causal sub-process.

Does 'enduring obligation relation' refer specifically to the ContractualObligation as a role-bearer dyad (e.g., the creditor–debtor relation), suggesting a relational structure rather than a simple quality? If so, should we mint a working:ContractualRelation class typed as a generically dependent continuant?

Is BreachOfContract intended as a legal-domain class only, or does it also need to connect to a specific legal system (e.g., common law vs. civil law), affecting how NormValidationCriteria or LegalArchitecture relate to it?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts three ontological commitments: (1) that a breach of contract is a process (BFO_0000015), (2) that there is an enduring obligation relation (modeled as ContractualObligation, a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation role), and (3) that the breach disrupts that relation (modeled as ObligationDisruption, a Quality inhering in the obligation). BreachOfContract is typed as a Process subclass and linked to ContractualObligation via RO_0000057 (has participant). ObligationDisruption captures the resultant altered state of the obligation using RO_0000052 (inheres in). ContractualObligation reuses the existing LegalObligation class to avoid redundancy. Several open questions remain about the precise BFO typing of the disruption effect and the relational structure of the obligation.

entities.label: SpecificPerformance
entities.rationale: Specific performance is a type of legal remedy that unfolds in time as a judicial or enforcement process compelling a party to fulfill an obligation. It is a Process (BFO_0000015) because it is an occurrent that happens and brings about a change in the world.

entities.label: RemedyProcess

entities.label: ObligationRealization
entities.rationale: The realization of an obligation is the process by which the content of a LegalObligation (a realizable role) is actually carried out or fulfilled. relations.rationale: Specific performance is a subclass of the general remedy-process class.
